en: offers of marriage.
note: #6239 (slice 077) must end like 'Lately, the people around me keep bringing me'

en: But I have a sweetheart named Joseph,
so I have no wish to marry anyone else.
Oh, I wonder why Joseph won't come back
to me
I'm going to wait for Joseph in the park,
however long it takes
Do you think that's strange?
But it's the only thing I can do!
What brings you here at this hour?
There's one thing I wanted to ask you.
Will you go on waiting for your sweetheart
like this, for all the years to come?
Yes, I intend to.
Does the waiting not pain you?
It does pain me.
But it can't be helped. It's the only thing
I can do.
I see. Then by night, I shall free you
note: no used_in; read as PLAYER's reply after msg 247092 (ends '[PLAYER]'), continued by #6259

en: from that pain.
Free me, you say...?
No! What are you doing?!
Now you are a Dhampir who feels no pain.
Is that not something to be glad of?
I'm in a hurry right now.
I have to get to Alster Park
I'm meeting someone there.
I have an errand to run, so if you'll excuse me
Hello, Lily.
I really must be getting home now
note: followed by #2 '...' + #25 '.' (four dots unless #25 gets an empty variant for msg 247359)

en: I run into you so often, don't I?
So why can I never meet him, I wonder?
you see...
note: continues #6214 (slice 077), which must end with a comma or no punctuation

en: The one I'm waiting for, my beloved Joseph,
is a soldier.
He went to war, saying he'd be back in a year.
But that day came, and still he hasn't come
This may sound cruel, but he might
have forgotten about you
by now.
No. That simply isn't true!
I believe in Joseph.
Even if he's late, I know he'll come back
to me.
By night, I shall be your servant
and work for you
Hello. Oh, you're a new face.
I know! You want work on the farm, right?
It's harvest time, so we're very short-handed.
Every day keeps me busy, too. It's hard work!
And the children are still little.
Winter's nearly here, so I must prepare for it.
I've got to make jam while I can, and
put away nuts for later
Oh, I know you can buy just about anything
note: sentence cut across #6294-#6296 at matching points

en: in the shops these days. But on a farm like
ours, our motto is: make everything yourself!
We've had a bumper wheat crop this year!
Our wheat, you know, goes to the bakery
every year
Cleaning, washing, cooking
This time of year, lots of folks work the farm.
I have to look after them as well.
I'm everyone's mother, you might say.
If you're free, would you mind helping me
with my work, too?
What, you're busy?
Hee hee. I'm only joking.
Hello. Oh, aren't you a young one.
What, you're busy too?
Y-you!
How did you get in here
I'm sorry I frightened you.
I didn't really mean to come inside.
My mother died right after I was born
so I've always longed so very much
for a family
I see. You poor thing.
It's all right. I'm everyone's mother, after all.
Think of me as your mother,
note: continues in #6320 (slice 079), e.g. 'and lean on me all you like.'
